senses.gloss: f. (רָצַע) boring, esp. the boring through of the Hebrew bondsman’s ear (according to Ex. XXI, 6).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 1:2">Kidd. I, 2</cite> <he>הנרצע נקנה בר׳</he> the slave that has his ear bored through is taken possession of by the act of boring.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 17b:5">Ib. 17ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 15:17">Deut. XV, 17</cite>) <he>אתה … או אינו אלא לר׳</he> you say, ‘and also to thy maid-servant thon shalt do likewise’ refers to the outfit (of the released slave), may it not refer to the boring? Ib. 16ᵇ <he>אין ר׳ באשה</he> the law of boring through the ear does not apply to a woman. Ib. <he>יובל של ר׳</he> the jubilee year for the slave that had his ear bored through (having declined to go free in his seventh year); a. fr.
